keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1917, which Cliopatria lacks. The state's own land is the 1915 shape: 'Southern Romania, including Oltenia, Muntenia, Dobruja, and southern Moldavia, was now in the hands of the Central Powers', but occupied land stays the owner's and is hatched in the occupier's colour (ledger occupation pairs with principality-of-bulgaria for Dobruja and german-empire for Oltenia, Muntenia and Focsani, 1916-1918); the government sat at Iasi and the Armistice of Focsani was signed 9 December 1917. Bessarabia is not Romanian yet (Moldavian Democratic Republic, December 1917; union 9 April 1918). Corrected by the repair pass of 2026-11-01 (reviewer eu-18-g, blocking): the first version subtracted the occupied south, which contradicted rule 4, the 1916 keyframe and the 1918 keyframe that restores it with no event in between.

union.cliopatria: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia

correction.text: the Old Kingdom with Bessarabia; Bukovina and Transylvania are added by the November and December 1918 events

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1918: the Old Kingdom plus Bessarabia (union voted 9 April 1918 [27 March O.S.]; 'its union with Romania was proclaimed earlier in 1918'). Bukovina (28 November) and Transylvania (1 December) join through the ledger so that the year's end equals Cliopatria's 1919 Kingdom of Romania shape. Treaty of Bucharest, 7 May 1918: the Romanian Campaign page gives the terms ('Romania would lose all of Dobruja to Bulgaria' and 'all the Carpathian passes to Austria-Hungary', with its oil leased to Germany for 99 years); 'The parliament signed the treaty, but King Ferdinand refused to sign it', and it 'was nullified by the terms of the Armistice of Compiegne' on 11 November 1918. No loss is recorded here: the king never signed, the land stayed Romanian (hatched as occupied, see the Dobruja and Wallachian pairs), and the nullification came six months later. principality-of-bulgaria records a 1918-5 gain of Southern Dobruja from this slug at confidence 2 (and a Neuilly loss in 1919-11); reading for eu-18 (Bulgaria): that gain is a paper transfer that never took effect, to be read with the occupation pair, not a change of owner. Repair pass 2026-11-01 (reviewer eu-18-g); the earlier note said the page gave no terms.

region.text: Cuza elected ruling prince of both Moldavia and Wallachia

ledger.note: 5 February 1859 (24 January O.S.): Alexandru Ioan Cuza is elected prince of both Moldavia and Wallachia, creating the personal union. The page gives no frontier; the core is Cliopatria's 1859 shape (both principalities, Southern Bessarabia included). Bucharest and Iasi share the capital role until 1862.
February 1859: Wallachia joins the union with Moldavia under Cuza; the Wallachia dossier ends with the same event.
February 1859: Moldavia joins the union with Wallachia under Cuza.

region.cliopatria: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia
region.text: both united principalities, Southern Bessarabia included (Cliopatria's 1859 shape, valid to 1877)

ledger.note: 5 February 1859: the union keeps the Ottoman suzerainty. The infobox reads 'Vassal state of the Ottoman Empire (1859-1877)' (footnote: 'De facto independent state'); 'Their separate autonomous vassalage in the Ottoman Empire continued with the unification of both principalities', and 'the suzerainty of the Sublime Porte had become a legal fiction'. The Kingdom of Romania page: 'Romania was still nominally a vassal of the Ottoman Empire'. The page gives the years, not the month; February is the union (found event). Added in the repair pass of 2026-11-01 (reviewer eu-18-g). The Ottoman dossier (me-10) has no vassal_start for this slug: its 1878 vassal_end events point to principality-of-wallachia and principality-of-moldavia, whose dossiers end in 1859, and should be re-pointed here.
3 February 1862 (22 January O.S.): the two principalities formally unite as the Romanian United Principalities and 'Bucharest becomes the sole capital, having shared the role with Iasi from 1859'.

13 July 1866: the first constitution takes effect and gives the state the name 'Romania'; Carol of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen had entered Bucharest on 22 May 1866 after Cuza's forced abdication in February 1866. 'Internationally, that name was used only after 1877-78.'

21 May 1877 (9 May O.S.): Romania proclaims full independence from the Ottoman suzerain; 'The Ottoman Empire later recognized this in the Treaty of San Stefano' and the powers at Berlin in 1878. The land does not change. Repair 2026-11-01: the vassalage is now a ledger pair of this dossier (vassal_start 1859-2, vassal_end 1877-5); the Ottoman dossier ends its vassalage in July 1878 against the Wallachia and Moldavia slugs.

region.text: the whole state, as at the start

ledger.note: 21 May 1877 (9 May O.S.): 'Romania proclaimed itself fully independent' and the infobox closes the vassalage in 1877. The pages differ on the legal end: 'The Ottoman Empire finally recognized Romanian independence in the Treaty of San Stefano' and the powers recognised it 'under the 1878 Treaty of Berlin' (13 July 1878, the date the Ottoman dossier uses). Confidence 2 because the year and day are the page's proclamation while the legal end is a matter of reading. Added in the repair pass of 2026-11-01.

13 July 1878: Southern Bessarabia goes back to Russia. The Treaty of Berlin, 'signed on 13 July 1878', made Romania 'cede southern Bessarabia to the Russian Empire'. (The United Principalities page dates the exchange '13 June 1878'.)

intersect.cliopatria: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia

ledger.note: 13 July 1878: Romania receives Dobruja. 'In compensation it received Dobruja, including the Danube Delta'; Cliopatria draws the land from 1880 and only the northern part (49 cells of the region's 83).

March 1881: Romania becomes a kingdom. The Kingdom page says parliament raised the country to kingdom status on 15 March 1881 and Carol was crowned on 10 May (its infobox gives 10 May 1881; the United Principalities infobox gives 14 March 1881 and 22 May in the text).

region.text: Dobruja: Southern Dobruja from 1 September 1916 (Turtucaia, 6 September), Constanta by 22 October

ledger.note: 1 September 1916: Mackensen's army 'attacked north from Bulgaria, starting on 1 September'; 'Bulgarian troops (aided by the German-Bulgarian Detachment) surrounded and stormed the fortress of Turtucaia' and 'The Romanian garrison surrendered on 6 September'; Constanta was 'occupied by the Central Powers on 22 October'. The page does not split Dobruja between Bulgarian and German control, so the whole region goes to Bulgaria, as its dossier does (occupation_start 1916-9). Split out of the former 'Central Powers' event by the repair pass of 2026-11-01 (reviewer eu-18-g). Confidence 2: date and land are the page's, the occupier is the researcher's reading (Mackensen's force was the Bulgarian Third Army, a German brigade and two divisions).

region.text: Oltenia, entered at Craiova on 21 November 1916

ledger.note: 21 November 1916: 'the German cavalry entered Craiova'. Oltenia is the first of the Wallachian lands to fall. Split out of the former 'Central Powers' event by the repair pass of 2026-11-01; the German Empire (a polities.csv slug of group eu-20, no dossier yet) is the counterpart because the page names Falkenhayn's and Mackensen's German armies, with Bulgarian, Austro-Hungarian and Ottoman troops beside them.

region.text: Muntenia, with Bucharest (fell 6 December 1916) and the Ploiesti oil fields

ledger.note: 6 December 1916: 'Bucharest was captured on 6 December by Falkenhayn's cavalry'; by the end of the year 'Southern Romania, including Oltenia, Muntenia, Dobruja, and southern Moldavia, was now in the hands of the Central Powers'; 'The Germans were able to repair the oil fields around Ploiesti'. Written from the occupied state's side (counterpart = occupier). Split out of the former 'Central Powers' event by the repair pass of 2026-11-01.

December 1916: the government leaves for Iasi. The 'Romanian government, royal court and public authorities' relocated to Iasi (the Kingdom page: 'Iasi (1916-1918)'); the month is the researcher's reading of the sequence after the fall of Bucharest.

region.text: the Focsani area of southern Moldavia, taken on 8 January 1917, behind the Siret line

ledger.note: 8 January 1917: 'Mackensen's troops were able to capture Focsani on 8 January' (the year follows the page's Brăila entry of 5 January 1917), but 'an attempt to break the Siret River line on 19 January failed'; the Romanian line then held in Vrancea (Marasti 24 July 1917, Marasesti to 3 September 1917). This replaces the former 40 km Galati radius, which the page does not mention. The 25 km radius is the researcher's reading of 'southern Moldavia' held by the Central Powers, so confidence 2. Repair pass 2026-11-01.
1918: the capital returns from Iasi to Bucharest ('Bucharest (1881-1916, 1918-1947); Iasi (1916-1918)').

9 April 1918 (27 March O.S.): Bessarabia joins Romania. 'On April 9 [O.S. March 27] 1918, Sfatul Tarii decided with 86 votes for, 3 against and 36 abstaining'; the union was conditional on agrarian reform, local autonomy and universal human rights (Sfatul Tarii later dropped the conditions). The Moldavian Democratic Republic was proclaimed on 15 December [2 December O.S.] 1917 and declared independence on 6 February [24 January O.S.] 1918. Counterpart set by reviewer eu-18-g: the Kingdom of Romania page has the 'Sfatul Tarii, or National Council' proclaim the union and lists the Moldavian Democratic Republic in its infobox succession; no dossier yet (counterparts_needing_dossiers). The Romanian Campaign page adds that 'the Central Powers recognized Romania's union with Bessarabia' (the May 1918 treaty) and that Bessarabia 'voted for union with Romania in April 1918'. Day and month added by the repair pass of 2026-11-01 from the Union of Bessarabia page; the Kingdom page still gives only 1918. Region 'Bessarabia' is the whole historical region, as in the 1918 keyframe.

November 1918: the Bulgarian hold on Dobruja ends with the nullification of the May treaty. Pages opened: Romania 're-entered the war' on 10 November 1918, 'one day before the German armistice' (Kingdom page: 'a day before the war ended in Western Europe'), and the Treaty of Bucharest 'was nullified by the terms of the Armistice of Compiegne' on 11 November 1918; neither says when the Central Powers' troops left, so the month bridges that silence (confidence 1). The Bulgarian dossier (eu-18) ends its occupation of Dobruja at Neuilly, 1919-11, also at confidence 1: that date lies outside this dossier's life (it closes in December 1918), so the pair is closed here at the nullification; the Bulgarian group or the kingdom-of-romania dossier should reconcile the two.

November 1918: the German hold on Oltenia ends. Pages opened: Romania 're-entered the war' on 10 November 1918, 'one day before the German armistice' (Kingdom page: 'a day before the war ended in Western Europe'), and the Treaty of Bucharest 'was nullified by the terms of the Armistice of Compiegne' on 11 November 1918; neither says when the Central Powers' troops left, so the month bridges that silence (confidence 1).

November 1918: the German hold on Muntenia and Bucharest ends. Pages opened: Romania 're-entered the war' on 10 November 1918, 'one day before the German armistice' (Kingdom page: 'a day before the war ended in Western Europe'), and the Treaty of Bucharest 'was nullified by the terms of the Armistice of Compiegne' on 11 November 1918; neither says when the Central Powers' troops left, so the month bridges that silence (confidence 1).

November 1918: the German hold on the Focsani area ends. Pages opened: Romania 're-entered the war' on 10 November 1918, 'one day before the German armistice' (Kingdom page: 'a day before the war ended in Western Europe'), and the Treaty of Bucharest 'was nullified by the terms of the Armistice of Compiegne' on 11 November 1918; neither says when the Central Powers' troops left, so the month bridges that silence (confidence 1).
28 November 1918: Bukovina joins Romania. 'Bukovina: Union declared 28 November 1918.'

region.text: Transylvania, declared united with Romania at Alba Iulia

ledger.note: 1 December 1918: Transylvania joins Romania. 'Transylvania: Union declared 1 December 1918 at Alba Iulia.'

December 1918: the Old Kingdom becomes Greater Romania. This dossier's span ends where Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Romania' row begins (1919); the state, its king and its colour continue (Kingdom page: 295,049 km2 in 1940 'including territories later ceded').

notes:
Five pages including two reused (Berlin, opened for the Montenegro dossier; Bucharest 1913, for the Greek). Cliopatria's 'United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia' row (1859-1916) is in fact the whole Old Kingdom of Romania (Principality of Romania from 1866, Kingdom from 1881); the dossier keeps the Cliopatria slug and carries the names as renames. It also extends over 1917-1918 with two new keyframes, because Cliopatria has no Romania between 1916 and 1919 and the state kept the Iasi government and the unoccupied north; it ends in December 1918, where Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Romania' row (1919-1947, slug kingdom-of-romania) begins. The dissolve event of 1918 is therefore a technical close (confidence 1). The Kingdom of Romania dossier may start at 1881 and overlap this one; the orchestrator should reconcile (the two rows share the colour family balkans and the state).

Cliopatria points proposed: the 1859 shape ends 1877 and the 1880 shape starts 1878 (Berlin, 13 July 1878); the 1916 shape is a composite (Transylvanian peak, minus Southern Dobruja) and should be replaced by the 1915 shape plus occupation events. Not settled: the Ottoman suzerainty of 1859-1877 is not on a page opened here (the Ottoman dossier records vassal_start/vassal_end for 'Wallachia' and 'Moldavia'); the holder of Bessarabia in 1918; whether Southern Bessarabia (Cahul, Bolgrad, Ismail) came to Moldavia in 1856: no page opened gives the Treaty of Paris, only Berlin's 'cede southern Bessarabia'; the terms of the May 1918 Treaty of Bucharest; Cliopatria's 1900 and 1915 small changes. The occupation events of 1916-1918 are written from the occupied state's side (counterpart = occupier), as the Serbs dossier does; the mirror belongs to the occupiers' dossiers. Area checks: 1915 shape 138,435 km2 against the Kingdom infobox 137,903 km2 for 1915 (1.00); Southern Dobruja 6,960 km2 against 7,989 km2 added by the 1913 shape (1.15).

Gazetteer: 'Budjak' is the gazetteer's alias for Southern Bessarabia; Galati radius 40 km stands for southern Moldavia.

Repair pass 2026-11-01 (reviewer eu-18-g): (1) the 1917 keyframe is now the whole 1915 shape, the occupation being drawn from the ledger (rule 4); (2) Ottoman suzerainty is a ledger pair (vassal_start 1859-2, vassal_end 1877-5, counterpart ottoman-empire) from the United Principalities page, with the legal end of 1878 left to the Ottoman dossier; (3) the former 'Central Powers' pair is split into Bulgaria (Dobruja, 1916-9) and german-empire (Oltenia 1916-11, Muntenia 1916-12, Focsani 1917-1) with ends in 1918-11 at confidence 1 because no page dates the withdrawal; the Galati radius is gone; (4) the 1918 keyframe states the terms and fate of the May 1918 Treaty of Bucharest and why no loss is recorded; (5) the Bessarabian union is dated 9 April 1918. Left as it was: the Bukovina and Transylvania gains with counterpart austria-hungary (eu-20 decides whether that dossier reaches November 1918 or the counterpart becomes the Hungarian state); the technical dissolve at confidence 1 against kingdom-of-romania (eu-21).
